full_text_en:
Weihai Kunpeng Investment Co., Ltd. v. Weihai Xigang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. and Shandong Key Construction Industry Co., Ltd. — jurisdictional objection in a land use rights dispute

【Ruling Summary】

To determine whether two lawsuits filed based on the same dispute constitute duplicative litigation, a comprehensive analysis shall be conducted in light of the specific claims and their bases, as well as the specific circumstances under which the parties exercise their rights of disposition. If the parties in the two lawsuits are different, the specific claims are also different, and they cannot substitute for or cover each other, the people's court may not simply deem the second lawsuit as duplicative because it arises from the same dispute, and dismiss it under the principle of "no second action for the same matter".

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2005) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 86

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Weihai Kunpeng Investment Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 9 Haibin North Road, Weihai City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Liu Changshui, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Liu Jinghong, lawyer of Shandong Huatian Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Weihai Xigang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 315 Shenyang Road, Weihai City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Miao Yanfei, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Meng Ying, lawyer of Shandong Jueping Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Shandong Key Construction Industry Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 46 Jingwu Xiaowei 4th Road, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhao Xianqing, Chairman of the Board.

The appellant Weihai Kunpeng Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kunpeng Company), in the case of a dispute over land use rights against the appellee Weihai Xigang Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xigang Company) and the third party at first instance Shandong Key Construction Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Key Construction Company), appealed against the civil ruling (2005) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 8 of the Shandong High People's Court to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with law and conducted an inquiry on October 26, 2005, with the attendance of Liu Jinghong, agent ad litem for Kunpeng Company, and Meng Ying, agent ad litem for Xigang Company. This case is now concluded.

During the trial of this case at first instance, Xigang Company raised an objection within the response period, claiming that this case and the civil case (2005) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 5 of the Shandong High People's Court were based on the same substantive subject matter and the same contractual facts, and that the acceptance of this case by the court of first instance constituted duplicative docketing. Kunpeng Company responded in the first instance that this case was an action for payment, while the case (2005) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 5 of the Shandong High People's Court was an action for confirmation, and that the acceptance of this case by the court of first instance did not constitute duplicative docketing.

Upon review, the court of first instance found: The case of Kunpeng Company v. Xigang Company and Key Construction Company over a land use rights dispute (hereinafter referred to as Civil Case No. 8) and the case of Xigang Company v. Kunpeng Company over a real estate development cooperation contract dispute, docketed on May 26, 2005 (hereinafter referred to as Civil Case No. 5), shared the same parties, the same facts, and the same legal relationship. 1. In terms of parties: although the case of Kunpeng Company v. Xigang Company and Key Construction Company added Key Construction Company as a third party, no claim was asserted against it in the claims; in terms of legal status, Key Construction Company was a third party without independent claims; therefore, the parties in the two cases were essentially the same. 2. In terms of facts: regardless of whether it was Kunpeng Company suing Xigang Company over a land use rights dispute or Xigang Company suing Kunpeng Company over a real estate development cooperation contract dispute, the focus of the dispute between the parties was primarily the validity of the "Real Estate Development Cooperation Contract" signed on March 25, 2003; thus, the facts of the two cases were the same. 3. In terms of legal relationship: the disputes between Kunpeng Company and Xigang Company both revolved around the rights and obligations arising from one real estate development cooperation contract. Therefore, the two cases had the same parties, the same facts, and the same legal relationship. The claims of Kunpeng Company in this case should have been raised as a counterclaim in the case of Xigang Company v. Kunpeng Company over a real estate development cooperation contract dispute (Civil Case No. 5), which had already been docketed and tried by the court of first instance, with an application to add the third party, and heard together; it was unnecessary to file another lawsuit based on the same substantive subject matter and the same contractual facts. Kunpeng Company's act of filing another lawsuit increased the burden on the parties and wasted judicial resources, and also violated the principle under the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC that no action may be brought again on the same matter. The objection raised by Xigang Company was sustained. Accordingly, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and Article 139 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, ruled on August 29, 2005, to dismiss the lawsuit filed by Kunpeng Company against Xigang Company and Key Construction Company.

Kunpeng Company, dissatisfied with the ruling of the first instance, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. The contents set forth in the ruling of the first instance were inconsistent with the facts of the case; in the first instance, it had submitted an application on August 24, 2005, requesting that the third party be changed to a defendant and be held jointly and severally liable for compensation for the invalidity of the contract; 2. Pursuant to Article 139, paragraph 2, of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, a ruling dismissing a lawsuit should be signed by the trial judge and court clerk responsible for hearing the case, but the collegial panel of this case consisted of judges from the case-filing division, thus there was a procedural error; 3. The finding of duplicative docketing by the court of first instance was unfounded, because the court of first instance's determination that Kunpeng Company could file a counterclaim precisely indicated that this was not a case of duplicative litigation; 4. The nature of the litigation, the claims and their amounts, the subject matter of the litigation, the parties and their numbers, the legal facts, and the legal relationships in the two cases were all different, and they did not constitute duplicative litigation; 5. Kunpeng Company's lawsuit satisfied the requirements of Article 108 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, whereas the court of first instance relied on Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, which concerns objections to jurisdiction, and Article 139 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, which concerns circumstances where the conditions for filing a lawsuit are not satisfied, thus the application of law was erroneous.

Xigang Company responded, arguing: 1. The conclusions of Civil Case No. 5 and the civil case (2005) Wei Min Yi Chu Zi No. 28 of the Weihai Intermediate People's Court resolved the claims made by Kunpeng Company in this case, and Kunpeng Company's filing of this lawsuit constituted duplicative litigation; 2. The finding of duplicative litigation by the court of first instance was in conformity with the facts of the case and the law, and Kunpeng Company's claim for adding a defendant and changing the claim had no factual or legal basis; 3. The trial procedure of the court of first instance complied with the Interim Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Docketing of Cases by People's Courts; 4. Dismissing Kunpeng Company's lawsuit by the court of first instance did not deprive it of its right to sue, as Kunpeng Company could apply to add the third party in Civil Case No. 5 without needing to file a separate lawsuit.

This Court, upon trial, found: On May 25, 2005, Kunpeng Company filed a lawsuit against Xigang Company at the Weihai Intermediate People's Court, requesting confirmation that the "Real Estate Development Cooperation Contract" signed by them was valid, and requesting that Xigang Company go through the procedures to commence the cooperative project and pay the corresponding fees. On May 26, 2005, Xigang Company filed a lawsuit against Kunpeng Company at the Shandong High People's Court, requesting confirmation that the "Real Estate Development Cooperation Contract" between them was invalid. The Shandong High People's Court consolidated the two aforementioned lawsuits into Civil Case No. 5 and held a hearing on July 11, 2005. On July 25, 2005, Kunpeng Company filed this lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting that Xigang Company deliver the land use rights in accordance with their "Real Estate Development Cooperation Contract".

Before the expiration of the evidence submission period on August 24, 2005, Kunpeng Company submitted to the court of first instance an "Application to Add a Defendant and Change Claims", requesting that Key Construction Company, the third party, be changed to a defendant, and that a judgment be made declaring the "Cooperation Agreement" between Xigang Company and Key Construction Company invalid, and ordering Xigang Company and Key Construction Company to bear joint and several liability for compensation. The court of first instance received this application on August 25, 2005.

This Court holds: Whether this case constitutes duplicative litigation shall be comprehensively analyzed in light of the bases of the parties' claims and the specific circumstances under which they exercised their rights of disposition. In Kunpeng Company's "Application to Add a Defendant and Change Claims" dated August 24, 2005, it had already changed Key Construction Company to a defendant; therefore, the parties in this case and in Civil Case No. 5 were not identical. The claims of Kunpeng Company in Civil Case No. 5 were a joinder of an action for confirmation and an action for payment; however, the content of the payment claim in that case was different from the content of the action for payment filed by Kunpeng Company on July 25, 2005. The claims of Kunpeng Company in Civil Case No. 5 could not cover the claims of Kunpeng Company in this case. Moreover, Kunpeng Company had already changed the claims in this case to "request a judgment declaring the 'Cooperation Agreement' between Xigang Company and Key Construction Company invalid, and ordering Xigang Company and Key Construction Company to bear joint and several liability for compensation" in its "Application to Add a Defendant and Change Claims". Therefore, the claims in this case and in Civil Case No. 5 were also different. The ruling of the first instance, which found that Kunpeng Company's lawsuit violated the principle of no second action for the same matter under the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC and dismissed the lawsuit against Xigang Company and Key Construction Company, applied the law incorrectly and shall be corrected.

In summary, in accordance with Article 187 of the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the ruling is as follows:

1. The civil ruling (2005) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 8 of the Shandong High People's Court is set aside;

2. The Shandong High People's Court is instructed to try this case.

Presiding Judge: He Xiaorong

Judge: Zhang Yafen

Acting Judge: Song Chunyu

November 9, 2005

Clerk: Yu Wenjun
